title: Hulk Smash: No Banner only HULK Drops 177.86 and Turns Week 1 Into a Statement
dek: Ramon's team opened 2026 with a 79-point demolition of Dawgs, Randy's Bears-fueled offense flattened Jordan, Zoe won her fantasy debut, and Sonny edged Alan by four points.
body: The eight-team era of the Buckaroo Football League is one week old, and somebody has already left a crater. Ramon's No Banner only HULK dropped 177.86 points on Mekhi's Dawgs, who managed 98.36, for a 79.5-point margin in a game the model actually leaned toward Dawgs at 54%. Before kickoff, Ramon's title odds sat at 11%, sixth-best in the league. After it, they sit at 47%, and every other manager is staring at that number the way you stare at a parking ticket.

The damage came from three directions at once. Josh Allen threw up 35.66 against a 19.32 projection, a rare moment when Brucie's adopted Bills loyalty paid out in actual points. Kenneth Walker III added 32.6 and D'Andre Swift chipped in 31.9, which means a Chicago running back helped beat a roster full of Chicago guys. The scariest part is that the Texans D/ST posted -4 and the team still cleared 177, so the HULK can apparently spot opponents a negative score and keep walking.

Mekhi, meanwhile, had a week to forget. Ja'Marr Chase delivered 2.2 points on a 16.44 projection, and Christian Watson put up 29.7 on the bench, a swap that would have been worth 27.5 points. To be fair to Kai, even the perfect lineup only gets Dawgs to about 125.86, nowhere near enough. His title odds went from 17%, tied for the best in the league, to 1%, which is the steepest one-week fall on the board.

Randy's The fumblers delivered the other blowout, a 146.16 to 75.96 rout of Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV. Caleb Williams was the week's top scorer at 37.26 against a 16.39 projection, and Derrick Henry added 34.8, so Randy's Bears devotion finally came with a box score to brag about. The same team got a flat zero from Colston Loveland, proof that Chicago football giveth and taketh in the same afternoon. Jordan's numbers are the grim kind: Ashton Jeanty scored 29.7 from the bench, and even with him active Counting or not Counting GV would have finished about 40 points short.

The most fun result belongs to the rookie. Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Kaushal's Habibsters 129.56 to 108.6 in her first-ever fantasy game, overcoming a 48% pregame projection and doing it with David Montgomery's 27.4 points parked on her bench. Winning while leaving that much on the pine is either a red flag or a warning to the rest of the league, and right now it looks like a warning. Kaushal's title odds plunged from 17% to 3%, and his only move of the week was swapping the Browns D/ST for the Jaguars D/ST, which feels like changing the tires after the engine cuts out.

The closest game of the week went to the commissioner. Sonny's The Horse is Hea held off Alan's Team Pillbert 106.42 to 102.1, a 4.32-point escape as a slight underdog at 46%. Jahmyr Gibbs gave Philly 31.1, but it wasn't enough to keep the bad guy from losing on opening day. Oddly, Sonny won and still watched his title odds slip from 9% to 4%, so he made a tight end move, adding Mark Andrews and dropping T.J. Hockenson.

The standings already have a shape. No Banner only HULK leads at 47% title odds and 98% playoff odds, The fumblers sit second at 28% and 93%, and Ghostu-Spider SZN holds steady at 13% with 76% playoff odds. Below that, everyone is in single digits, and Jordan's team is at 0% for the title and 3% for the playoffs after one week, which is a statistical way of saying there is a lot of season left to prove the computer wrong.

Week 2 serves up the game of the week right away: Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN against Ramon's No Banner only HULK, two unbeatens with the rookie taking on the juggernaut. Mekhi gets Randy's The fumblers, a chance to climb out of a hole against a team that just scored 146. Alan and Kaushal meet in a battle of 0-1 teams whose odds evaporated in one weekend, and Jordan draws Sonny looking for a first win. Somebody stop Ramon, or at least make him sweat.

bios.1: Sonny squeaked past Alan 106.42 to 102.1 as a slight underdog, then swapped T.J. Hockenson for Mark Andrews. Despite the win, title odds dipped from 9% to 4%. A matchup with winless Jordan offers a chance to build on it.
bios.2: Randy's squad hung 146.16 on Jordan behind Caleb Williams' week-best 37.26 and Derrick Henry's 34.8. Title odds nearly doubled to 28%, even with a goose egg from Colston Loveland. Dawgs come next, desperate for a win.
bios.3: Jordan's team posted the week's low score at 75.96 while Ashton Jeanty's 29.7 sat on the bench. The model now gives 0% title odds and 3% playoff odds, which means there's nowhere to go but up. Sonny is the first chance to prove the math wrong.
bios.4: Alan got 31.1 from Jahmyr Gibbs and still lost by 4.32 to the commissioner. Title odds slid from 14% to 4%, with playoff odds at 32%. Next week's game against Kaushal is a chance to start digging out.
bios.5: Mekhi's preseason co-favorite managed 98.36 and lost by 79.5, sunk by Ja'Marr Chase's 2.2 and Christian Watson's 29.7 on the bench. Title odds fell from 17% to 1%, the biggest drop in the league. A date with Randy's red-hot offense is next.
bios.6: Kaushal's 108.6 fell 21 points short of a rookie, and the title odds crashed from 17% to 3%. The response so far is a defense swap, Jaguars in and Browns out. Alan awaits in a meeting of 0-1 teams.
bios.7: Ramon's team opened with a league-best 177.86, a 79.5-point flattening of Dawgs powered by Josh Allen, Kenneth Walker III, and D'Andre Swift. Title odds rocketed from 11% to 47%, and the playoffs sit at 98%. Next up is an unbeaten Zoe with everyone watching.
bios.8: Zoe won her first-ever fantasy game, 129.56 to 108.6 over a two-time champion, despite leaving David Montgomery's 27.4 on the bench. The odds held steady at 13% for the title and 76% for the playoffs. Week 2 brings a showdown with the league's hottest team.
